title: Design for the Cast Iron Gate of Castle ‘s-Gravenwezel (Belgium)
creator: Jan Pieter van Baurscheidt the Younger
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edward Pearce Casey Fund, 2016 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Pen and grey wash elevation of a cast-iron estate gate with two urn-topped piers and scrollwork. Symmetric, clean, centered; cream paper so easy luminance key. Use whole gate as the garden gate hero or split piers and gate leaf into layers.

title: The door of a grotto
creator: William Marlow
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Jeffrey L. Berenson and Raymond Lifchez Living Trust Gifts, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: William Marlow watercolour: the door of a grotto set into craggy rock. A real grotto entrance in soft blue and ochre; vignette edge on paper, so key by paper tone and soften the edge.

title: Fishermen by Moonlight
creator: Joseph Vernet
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1953 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Blue-toned aquatint of fishermen by a moonlit river bank with a big tree and cottage, c. 1750-1800. Soft teal with a lit moon: tree and water layers could be separated. Small figures in a boat.

title: 'De Fontein van de Koninglijke door-eengevlochte Naam; voor de veiver', in: Tooneel Der Voornaamste Nederlands Huizen, En Lust Hoven, Naar T Leven Afgebeeld
creator: Carel Allard
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1937 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured print of a sunken stepped basin fountain in a park. Soft rose, green and blue tints; has book spine and margins, crop to the plate.

title: Design for a Gate
creator: Anonymous, French, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Harvard Arnason, 1971 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Fine pen and wash elevation of a gate between two rusticated piers with an ironwork overthrow and cartouche. Very clean outline, plain cream ground, easy cutout. Piers can be a separate layer from the iron leaf.

title: A Fountain in a Grotto
creator: Giovanni Guerra
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, James A. and Maria R. Warth Gift, in memory of Anne and Peter Warth, 1999 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Brown wash drawing of a fountain in a shell-niched grotto with rusticated surround, octagonal sheet. Warm and strong silhouette; contains reclining figures as sculpture, crop or paint out if needed.

title: Tintern Abbey by moonlight
creator: John "Warwick" Smith
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Malcolm Hewitt Wiener Foundation and Jill Newhouse Gifts, 2003 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Tintern Abbey by moonlight, tinted print c. 1789: ruin on a hillside over a river with gentle moon glow. Calm background layer; no foreground figures that matter.

title: Design for a Cartouche, plate 2 from "Neü inventierte sehr dienstiche Schilde oder Cartouches"
creator: Jeremias Wachsmuth
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Daniel Ergmann Gift, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hofer rococo cartouche with an empty centre, plate printed c. 1750-56, in an album with a leather edge to crop. Symmetric empty frame ready for label text.

title: Design for Gate Piers with Paired Pilasters and Domed Caps, and a Gate
creator: Anonymous, British, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Elisha Whittelsey Collection, The Elisha Whittelsey Fund, 1949 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Faint wash design for gate piers with domed caps and a spear-topped iron leaf. Light line weight so it needs a strong levels pass; shape is simple and elegant for a small side gate.

title: View of a Palace Garden with a Central Pond Surrounded by Classical Architecture (Tapestry or Stage Design?)
creator: Daniel Marot the Elder
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Brooke Russell Astor Bequest, 2013 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Watercolour of a palace garden seen between columns with urns and statue plinths on balustraded terraces. Tinted, painterly, usable as a mid-ground layer; urns and balustrade could be harvested. Statues are minor figures.

title: View of the Menagerie at Kew
creator: Thomas Sandby
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Watercolour View of the Menagerie at Kew (1763): a small pagoda pavilion on a curved pond edge with trees, pale blue wash water. Pond edge, reflection and pavilion in one; vignette edge, plain paper around.

title: Design for a Cartouche, plate 6 from "Neü inventierte sehr dienstiche Schilde oder Cartouches"
creator: Jeremias Wachsmuth
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Daniel Ergmann Gift, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hofer rococo cartouche, empty centre, shell crest. Album page with leather edge; the frame is isolated on paper.

title: Bronze Garden Vase with Two Putti from the Gardens of Versailles
creator: Claude Ballin the Elder
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edward Pearce Casey Fund, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Pen and grey wash drawing of a bronze garden vase with two putti, from the gardens of Versailles. Plain paper, centered object, clean silhouette: ideal urn on a pier. Faint grid lines in the paper to remove.

title: Study of a Tree in the Luxembourg Gardens
creator: Pierre Henri de Valenciennes
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, The Isaacson-Draper Foundation Gift, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Red-chalk study of a forked trunk in the Luxembourg Gardens, 1773. Foreground framing trunk candidate with branching top; warm red already fits the palette. Mounted in a gold-edged mat: crop it.

title: Trade Card of John Roker, Goldsmith
creator: Anonymous, British, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Morris Hawkes, 1927 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Trade card with an ornamental border and urn, framing a text block (John Roker). Ephemera feel; keep the border and urn, blank the text for a plant label or card.

title: Design for a Grotto with a Fountain
creator: Anonymous, Italian, 17th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Elisha Whittelsey Collection, The Elisha Whittelsey Fund, 1961 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Pen and wash design for a grotto niche with a tiered fountain, touched with blue wash on the water. Rusticated stone arch is a grotto entrance candidate; stained paper, plain around the object.

title: Vauxhall Garden
creator: Thomas Rowlandson
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1917 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured aquatint of Vauxhall Garden lit at night, lanterns glowing under tall trees (1809). Dark sky, warm lights: strong mood plate. Tiny strolling figures are present, small and period; use as far-background or crop to trees and pavilion.

title: The Villa Torlonia, from the original painting by Joseph Castiglione in the collection of Mrs. A. T. Stewart, New York
creator: Edmond Yon
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Ellen Robinson, 1960 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Villa Torlonia engraving with a pond edged by a stone balustrade under big trees. Dense dark foliage mass; balustrade and pond usable as a foreground. Contains a few seated figures.

title: Doorway and Vine
creator: James McNeill Whistler (American, 1834–1903)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Ralph King (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Whistler etching of a dark vaulted doorway through a vine-covered wall into light beyond. Mood piece for a wall opening: cut out the arch as an alpha hole or keep as a dark passage layer. Mid cutout difficulty.

title: The Doorway
creator: James McNeill Whistler (American, 1834–1903)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Bequest of James Parmelee (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Whistler etching of an arched lattice (trellis) doorway in a stone wall. Good as a garden doorway or arbour entrance; the lattice is fine detail so edges need care. Portrait format.

title: The Garden
creator: James McNeill Whistler (American, 1834–1903)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Ralph King (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Whistler etching The Garden: weathered door at the top of garden steps. Usable for door plus steps; heavy plate-tone so key by luminance and keep the paper warm.

title: The Fountains of Rome (Le fontane di Roma), Book IV, plate 21: View of the Cascade below the Organ from the Garden (Veduta della Cascata Sotto L'Organo nel Piano del Giardino)
creator: Giovanni Francesco Venturini (Italian, 1650–1710)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Jean Corser (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Venturini etching from Le fontane di Roma: a cascade falling from a grotto-like wall in a garden under trees. Full-sheet scene with plain margin; strong for fountain or grotto mood. Black-and-white, would be tinted.

title: Cedar (Cedrus sp.): tree with separate segments of cones and leaves. Coloured engraving by J.J. or J.E. Haid, c.1750, after G.D.Ehret.
creator: Georg Dionysius Ehret
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Hand-coloured engraving of a cedar of Lebanon with cones and seed scales around it, on plain paper. Beautiful conifer silhouette with horizontal tiers; cones can be used as separate hanging ornaments. Easy cutout.

title: Oak tree (Quercus hindsii) with person lying at its base. Coloured lithograph, c.1857.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Chromolithograph of a broad oak tree in warm autumn gold with a second tree behind, plain pale ground. Soft rich colour, big open canopy, trunk visible: good single tree for perching birds. Paper key then clean the grass base.

title: An old oak tree (Quercus robur) with surrounding vegetation. Lithograph, c. 1822.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Lithograph of an old oak with open, twisted branching and visible sky gaps, on plain paper (corner dog-ear and page edge to trim). Good silhouette for swallows; monochrome so tint by layer.

title: The Physic Garden, Chelsea: a view towards the river showing the cedars by the wall. Lithograph by H. Warren after J. Fuge.
creator: Fuge, James, -1838.
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Lithograph: south view of the cedars of Lebanon in the Apothecaries Physic Garden at Chelsea, flat layered crowns along a path. A garden-tree scene with a plain paper margin; the two big cedars can be cut from the ground.

title: Monterey Cypress
creator: Ernest Haskell (American, 1876–1925)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Bequest of Mrs. Henry A. Everett for the Dorothy Burnham Everett Memorial Collection (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Lithograph of two gnarled, wind-bent bare cypress trees on tan paper. Strange and open branching, ideal perches; dark ink on toned paper so key by luminance.

title: The Cypress Grove
creator: Samuel Palmer (British, 1805–1881)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Lewis B. Williams, presented in honor of Henry Sayles Francis, Curator of Prints (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Etching of a dark cypress and cedar grove with a stream. Heavy dark masses for silhouette trees at the garden edge; dense so cutout is mostly a luminance key and mass shape.

title: Eight Views of Kanazawa at Night
creator: Utagawa Hiroshige (Japanese, 1797–1858)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Francis F. Prentiss for the Dudley P. Allen Collection (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hiroshige triptych of Kanazawa at night: low islands in a bay under a full moon, deep blue woodblock gradients. Wide far-background layer, 3 panels that join; soft colour, no text beyond cartouches.

title: The Monkey Bridge
creator: Katsushika Taito II (Japanese, active c. 1810–50s)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift from J. H. Wade (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Woodblock of an arched Monkey Bridge under a full moon over a river gorge, early 1830s. Blue night colour with a moon disc behind the arch: reads as a ready moonlit window shot.

title: Moonlight on the Medway at Chatham
creator: Frank Short (British, 1857–1945)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of John Bonebrake (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Mezzotint-style Moonlight on the Medway: warm sepia night sky with a moon, dark shore and a sail. Quiet, low-key far layer that holds colour tinting well.

title: Cedar trees (Cedrus species) in a garden in Monmouthshire. Photogravure by R. Fenton, ca. 1856.
creator: Roger Fenton
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Engraving of cedar trees reflected in a still pond (Cedrus, 1856). Clean water reflection on plain paper, monochrome, good for a pond layer with a tree beside it.

title: New Model for a Cartouche
creator: Stefano Della Bella (Italian, 1610–1664)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Dudley P. Allen Fund (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Stefano della Bella sheet of twelve empty cartouches and frames, 1647. Black ink on plain paper, each frame separable by grid; ideal for plant-label frames and Herbario cards.

title: Design for a Cartouche
creator: Gilles Marie Oppenord (French, 1672–1742)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, L. E. Holden Fund (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Oppenord red-chalk design for a cartouche: tall asymmetrical scrolls, warm red already in palette. Slim edge frame; plain paper.
